solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

parts.note: plastic in the sense of pliable, bending easily, is supple
potty is informal British for crazy, as is mental

explanation.surface: Someone has a spare plastic potty, perhaps for a toddler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plastic' and 'potty' look like adjective and noun describing a child's toilet; both are adjectives giving pieces, and 'Spare' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spare is extra, additional to what is needed, which is the sense of the adjective.

parts.note: to put on a feeling is to fake or sham it
ice in a drink is rocks, as in whisky on the rocks

explanation.surface: Some national symbols are being chilled on ice.
explanation.walkthrough: The trefoil leaf is the emblem of Ireland, worn on St Patrick's Day.
explanation.definitionFit: The three-leaved clover plant is the traditional symbol of Ireland, so several of them are national emblems.

parts.note: a hoard of money is a pile
one is the Roman numeral I; the 's stands for 'is', joining wordplay to definition

explanation.surface: Someone stockpiles their own hats.
explanation.walkthrough: PILEI is the plural of pileus, the botanical term for the cap of a mushroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanists call the umbrella-shaped top of a mushroom a pileus; several of these toadstool tops make the plural.

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see, as in lo and behold

indicators.note: short means the word loses its last letter, cut off at the end

parts.note: extremely means very

explanation.surface: Look at this admirer, who is very small.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' takes the last letter off VERY, leaving VER.
explanation.definitionFit: A suitor or sweetheart is an admirer, someone who adores another person.

clue.text: Ancient Greek enemy can, manoeuvring around area

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters sit on either side of the single letter for area
manoeuvring means the letters of the words enemy can are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: An enemy in antiquity manoeuvres a can around some territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvring' rearranges ENEMYCAN into MYCENEAN, which goes 'around' A. Mycenae was the city of Agamemnon in Bronze Age Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Mycenae, the Bronze Age citadel of Agamemnon, was an inhabitant of early Greece.

indicators.note: captures means one piece takes another inside it

parts.note: a pilot of aircraft is an aviator

explanation.surface: A fresh pilot takes a decent seaman prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'captures' puts G inside AVIATOR, giving AVIGATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A navigator steers a ship and is a seafarer; the great explorers were famous navigators.

indicators.note: on retirement means the letters go back, read from right to left in a down entry

parts.note: to express a view is to air it
ta is informal British for thank you

explanation.surface: Someone says thank you at their retirement party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on retirement' turns AIRTA around.
explanation.definitionFit: An atrium is an open central court in a Roman house; the plural gives several courtyards.

indicators.note: potentially suggests the letters of the quoted words could be something else once rearranged

explanation.surface: A philosophical remark that something might be brought into being.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potentially' rearranges ITISMADEREAL; and the result means made real, so the whole clue both builds and defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has taken physical form or come into existence has become actual, made real.

parts.note: giant as an adjective means very big, tall

explanation.surface: A giant appears in some fashion or other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giant' looks like a noun but is the adjective tall.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used for emphasis in negatives and questions, meaning to any extent or in any respect.

clue.text: Clubs always protected by plastic film

indicators.note: protected by means these pieces are held inside another, shielded

parts.note: plastic means a credit card, such as a Visa
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games
ever means always, as in ever hopeful

explanation.surface: Golf clubs are always wrapped in plastic film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plastic' means a credit card here, not wrapping, and 'film' is the definition: Vice Versa is a 1988 body-swap comedy. 'protected by' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Vice Versa is a 1988 comedy movie in which a father and son swap bodies.

indicators.note: nurses means holds close, carrying the other pieces inside

parts.note: a would-be star is an aspiring one
in means accepted or fashionable

explanation.surface: Trainee nurses ask whether they have been admitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nurses' looks like a noun for trainee carers; it is the verb, ASPIRING holding WE and IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something magnificent fills the onlooker with awe, so it is impressive or breathtaking.

clue.text: Far end of Alsace Lorraine rebuilt some time ago

indicators.note: far end of means only the final letter of the word Alsace is used
rebuilt means the letters are put together again in a new order

explanation.surface: A region of eastern France is reconstructed long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuilt' rearranges LORRAINE into ARLIERON, after the last letter of Alsace.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase refers to a previous moment, a while back, before the present point.

indicators.note: to secure means to hold the other piece fast inside

parts.note: to look steadily is to gaze
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Someone checks they can fasten a big overcoat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to secure' puts L inside GAZE.
explanation.definitionFit: A glaze is a thin shiny layer applied over pottery or food, a covering coat.

clue.text: Drunk Peruvian artist dismissed from lesson?

parts.note: the Inca were the ancient people of Peru

indicators.note: dismissed from means the artist is sent out of the word for lesson

parts.note: a parable is a story teaching a moral lesson
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: A tipsy painter from Peru is thrown out of class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissed from' removes RA from PARABLE, leaving PABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Drunk and incapable is a stock British police phrase; someone too intoxicated to function is helpless.

indicators.note: about means the word for alarm goes round the other pieces

parts.note: alarm or sudden fear is panic
a ram is a male sheep that butts, so a butter

explanation.surface: There is widespread alarm about old butter, a food scare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' is not the dairy spread but one who butts, a male sheep. 'about' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweeping, wide-ranging view takes in everything, broad and comprehensive.

clue.text: Way to cut open type of carpet

indicators.note: to cut means one piece slices into the other, sitting inside it

parts.note: a flower opens when it blooms
a way is a road

explanation.surface: Instructions on how to slice open a roll of carpet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'open' is a verb here, as a flower opens, and 'to cut' signals one piece slicing into the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Carpet woven on a wide loom, in one seamless piece, is called by this name.

clue.text: Single in resort city of Italy

indicators.note: in means the single letter goes inside the word for resort

parts.note: to resort to something is to turn to it
I is the Roman numeral one, a single

explanation.surface: A lone traveller visits a holiday resort city in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday town but is the verb turn. 'in' places I inside TURN.
explanation.definitionFit: Torino, the Piedmont capital and home of Fiat, is a major northern Italian city.

clue.text: To break concrete, picks up drill

indicators.note: to break means to split the other word, sitting in its middle

parts.note: concrete means real or actual, not abstract
to pick up a sound is to hear it

explanation.surface: A workman uses a drill to smash concrete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concrete' is the adjective meaning actual, not building material, and 'drill' is practice, not a tool. 'To break' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A practice run of a play or procedure is a drill, a run-through before the real thing.

clue.text: Antibody extremely likely to do bad

indicators.note: extremely means only the outermost letters, first and last, of likely

parts.note: to do wrong is to sin

explanation.surface: An antibody is very probably going to do harm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' looks like an intensifier for likely; it takes that word's ends, LY.
explanation.definitionFit: A lysin is an antibody or other agent that dissolves cells, so it is an antibody type.

clue.text: I simply have to have it

definitions.text: I simply have to have it

parts.words: I simply have to have it
parts.note: reads as a shopper's craving, but literally says that to have something is all it takes to possess it

explanation.surface: A shopper insists they must own some desirable item.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue sounds like desire; read flatly, having a thing is exactly what possession is.
explanation.definitionFit: Possession of a thing is simply having it, which is what holding title to property means.

clue.text: Oddly smug, for a senior cop

indicators.note: oddly means the first and third letters of smug are taken

parts.note: per means for each, as in miles per hour

explanation.surface: A senior police officer behaves in a strangely self-satisfied way.
explanation.walkthrough: A super is short for a superintendent, a senior police rank in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A superintendent is a high-ranking police officer, often shortened to this informal form.

parts.note: an irritating person or thing is a pest
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed about an Italian sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' looks like 'about'; it is the cricket abbreviation O.
explanation.definitionFit: This Genoese basil, pine nut and parmesan paste is a classic pasta dressing.

clue.text: Awful couple hiding son in poor condition

indicators.note: hiding means the other pieces conceal the letter for son within them

parts.note: awful means dire
a couple is a pair

explanation.surface: A terrible couple are concealing their son, who is in a bad way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hiding' signals that the letter for son sits inside the first piece, giving DISRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A building that has fallen into dilapidation is in a bad state, neglected and needing repair.

indicators.note: also means one more piece is added after the first

parts.note: a pig pen is a sty
LI is 51 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A list of writing pens and a count of fifty-one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' is an animal enclosure; 'pens' at the end are writing tools.
explanation.definitionFit: A stylus is a pointed writing instrument, so the plural means several writing implements.

parts.note: eg means for example, used to illustrate
to ret is to soak flax or hemp to soften it

explanation.surface: An example of soaking a pair of fishing waders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wader' is a long-legged bird, not boots.
explanation.definitionFit: This white heron of shallow waters is a classic wading bird.

parts.note: free spirits suggests carefree people, but means to release souls from their bodies

explanation.surface: A question about people who live unconventionally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free' is a verb here: to release a soul from its flesh.
explanation.definitionFit: To separate a soul from its body sets the spirit free of its physical form.

indicators.note: frames means the words pictures into hold the letters within them

explanation.surface: Instructions to glue pictures into their frames.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frames' looks like picture frames, but it is a verb: the letters sit inside 'pictures into'.
explanation.definitionFit: Resin, sticky tree sap or a synthetic polymer, is used as an adhesive.

clue.text: Guarded, but without being locked up?

parts.note: non means not or without, as a prefix
committal is the act of being sent to prison or an institution

explanation.surface: Someone cautious asks whether they avoided jail.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the fanciful reading: not being committed to prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A guarded reply gives nothing away, refusing to take a definite position.
